caption: The drawing depicts a single metal pitcher with a wide bulbous body, a smooth surface, and a scroll-decorated rim. The pitcher is depicted in pencil on a beige or light tan sheet of paper, with careful shading to denote the metallic surface and contours. The body of the pitcher narrows at the neck and then flares out at the lip, which sweeps upwards on one side to form a spout. There is a thin, angular handle attached to the back, rising from the upper body to just above the rim. Ornate etching or engraved patterns are present along the top edge of the pitcher, and a central decorative cartouche on the front displays a monogram or initials surrounded by a wreath-like motif. The bottom of the pitcher sits flat, and a small shadow is drawn beneath it. The sheet contains a double rectangular border, with the inner one more defined and containing the pitcher image, and the outer in a looser style with brownish stains or marks. In the upper left outside the border, the words "CASE #3" are written, and in the lower right are the notations "No. 18799-26 5 INCHES HIGH" along with a signature "Eugene Canill." The composition is centered on the pitcher, with all labeling and signature placed in the corners outside of the outlined border.
title: Silver Creamer
cluster: #19 — Ceramic Arts: Pottery, Stoneware, and Porcelain
